title: Environment-Based Configuration
learning_outcomes: Explain what environment-based configuration contributes to a PHP application.
Apply at least one of these concepts in a small example: development configuration.
Check one edge case and explain how to diagnose unexpected behavior.

content.intro: Production reliability includes repeatable builds, correct runtime configuration, secret separation, compatible migrations, health checks, logging, monitoring, and a rollback strategy—not only uploading source files. In this lesson, focus on development configuration; then compare it with environment variables. Use the example to predict a result before checking it, and record one case where the behavior may differ.
content.why_it_matters: You will use environment-based configuration when building readable, testable PHP programs. Its practical value is knowing which rule applies, what result to expect, and how to handle failure or unexpected input.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Production reliability includes repeatable builds, correct runtime configuration, secret separation, compatible migrations, health checks, logging, monitoring, and a rollback strategy—not only uploading source files. For environment-based configuration, begin with development configuration. Also distinguish environment variables; secret injection; per-environment database connections. Identify the input, the rule applied, and the observable output or side effect; then check the relevant official reference when a version or edge-case detail matters.

items.title: Development configuration
items.text: Know when to use development configuration, what input or program state it changes, and which boundary case is worth testing.

items.title: Environment variables
items.text: Know when to use environment variables, what input or program state it changes, and which boundary case is worth testing.

items.title: Secret injection
items.text: Treat the relevant value as untrusted, apply the defense at the correct boundary, and verify a deliberately invalid or hostile-looking input is rejected or encoded.

items.title: Per-environment database connections
items.text: Keep query structure separate from data values, check failures explicitly, and use constraints or transactions when integrity depends on multiple operations.

items.title: Validating required settings at startup
items.text: Know when to use validating required settings at startup, what input or program state it changes, and which boundary case is worth testing.

content_blocks.title: A small PHP example for Environment-Based Configuration
content_blocks.code:
<?php
$steps = ["begin transaction", "validate changes", "commit or roll back"];
echo implode(" -> ", $steps) . PHP_EOL;

content_blocks.title: Professional habit
content_blocks.text: Keep secrets outside build artifacts, run repeatable checks before rollout, and define health checks and rollback plans.

content_blocks.title: Walk through one example
content_blocks.text: Read the example for environment-based configuration from top to bottom. Start by identifying development configuration, write down the relevant variable values or control-flow choice, and predict the expected output before running it. Then change one input or condition, check a boundary case, and explain why the result changed.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a pattern without understanding its inputs and output.
common_mistakes.why: Small environment or type differences can change behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Trace one example by hand, name expected outputs, and consult version-matched official docs.

common_mistakes.problem: Ignoring empty, invalid, or boundary input.
common_mistakes.why: Real data rarely matches only the simplest example.
common_mistakes.fix: Add a deliberate edge-case check before relying on the result.

common_mistakes.problem: Making several changes at once while debugging.
common_mistakes.why: It becomes difficult to identify which change caused the behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Reduce the issue to one small reproducible case, change one cause, and retest.
